ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Frédéric Chopin — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Three months of cough, two weeks of blood-streaked sputum, night sweats, and weight loss: chest X-ray and CT, sputum samples, blood tests, home airborne isolation, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department

text.paragraph: Three months of cough, two weeks of blood-streaked sputum, night sweats, and weight loss: chest X-ray and CT, sputum samples, blood tests, home airborne isolation, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: He has coughed for about three months, now with streaks of blood, sweats at night, and has lost weight; he wants to know what is wrong. [S]
He teaches piano at home and performs; he wants to know when he can teach again and whether his students are at risk. [S]
He is afraid his students and neighbors will shun him if they learn he may have tuberculosis. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin was born in the village of Żelazowa Wola, in Mazovia, on March 1, 1810, according to his own statements and his family's; his baptismal certificate, written several weeks after the birth, gives February 22. [D]

His father, Mikołaj (Nicolas) Chopin, was a Frenchman from Lorraine who settled permanently in Poland and brought up his children as Poles; the family moved to Warsaw a few months after Fryderyk's birth. [D]
In 1827 the youngest of the Chopin children, his sister Emilia, died of tuberculosis. [D]
A review of the documentary sources reports recurrent episodes of cough, fever, headaches, and swollen lymph nodes beginning in his teens. [D]
He left Warsaw on November 2, 1830, never to return, reached Paris in September 1831, and in 1834 chose the status of a political refugee rather than apply to the Russian embassy for a passport. [D]

In Paris his most important source of income was giving lessons; he became a popular teacher, and although ranked among the greatest pianists of his time, he disliked public performances, appeared rarely, and preferred an intimate group of listeners. [D]

In 1836 a proposal of marriage was accepted on condition that he take better care of his health; the engagement ended a year later, the family of his fiancée being disturbed by the bad state of his health, as he had been seriously ill in the winter. [D]
He met the writer George Sand in Paris in 1836; their relationship, which began soon after, lasted nearly ten years. [D]

text.paragraph: 12 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

Alcohol: a glass of wine with dinner a few times a week (AUDIT-C 2); never smoked; no drug use; no incarceration, homelessness, or work in health care [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Quiet, courteous, and precise; organized thought; thin and tired. Mood low and anxious about the illness and his students; homesick; PHQ-9 7, with item 9 scored 0; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. list.item: Cough for about three months, blood-streaked sputum for two weeks, night sweats, and weight loss of about 6 kg in a man of 28, with a right upper lobe cavity on chest X-ray and CT: suspected pulmonary tuberculosis; home airborne isolation and three sputum samples for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification, and culture: active, confirmed [S]
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 16.8, about 11 percent weight loss in three months, and albumin 3.2 g/dL: active, confirmed [S]

Infectious diseases consultation to confirm the diagnosis, choose between the six-month and four-month regimens, plan monitoring and his return to teaching, and address cystic fibrosis and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency as explanations for his lifelong chest illness. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Interim Guidance: 4-Month Rifapentine-Moxifloxacin Regimen for the Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Pulmonary Tuberculosis - United States, 2022 (2022) [S]

Diagnosis: three sputum samples at least eight hours apart, one early in the morning, for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification with rifampin resistance, culture, molecular testing for isoniazid and fluoroquinolone resistance, and phenotypic susceptibility; an interferon-gamma release assay; HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests; and baseline blood count, liver and kidney tests, potassium, calcium, and magnesium. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Interim Guidance: 4-Month Rifapentine-Moxifloxacin Regimen for the Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Pulmonary Tuberculosis - United States, 2022 (2022) [S]

Infection control and public health: home airborne isolation with no students or visitors and a surgical mask around others; same-day report of suspected tuberculosis to the health department; a contact investigation of his students, friends, and other close contacts led by the health department. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Guidelines for the investigation of contacts of persons with infectious tuberculosis: recommendations from the National Tuberculosis Controllers Association and CDC (2005) [S]

Nutrition: two dietitian visits in the first month, three meals and three energy-dense snacks a day, two oral nutrition supplement drinks a day, and weight at every visit. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Consensus statement: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition: characteristics recommended for the identification and documentation of adult malnutrition (undernutrition) (2012) [S]

Support: plain information about how tuberculosis spreads, how quickly treatment makes him non-infectious, and that it is curable; help with what to tell his students; PHQ-9 at diagnosis, at two months, and at the end of treatment. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
